messages:
Elena (security): FYI I'm planning a small RBAC change for the buildkite-service account so it can decrypt SCA scan artifacts stored encrypted with our KMS. Need input on audit logging + canary plan. tagging @ram
Ram (infra): OK, what exact permission are you adding? kms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt or a key ring-level role?
Elena (security): proposing roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter at the key level (not keyring). snippet: ```gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding my-key --member=serviceAccount:buildkite-service@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter```
Tara (eng): quick Q: why not ephemeral grants via short-lived token? we try to avoid long-lived service perms if possible.
Elena (security): good point. buildkite workers need to run nightly SAST/DAST postprocessing across older artifacts; short-lived is a bit clunky with current runner setup. We can add a 90-day review cadence and a precise audit hook instead.
Ram (infra): For audit logs: enable CMEK data access logs + Cloud Audit Logs for key access. We should also push a structured entry to our logging pipeline when decrypt happens so it joins the scan evidence ID. Example event query for Cloud Logging: ```resource.type="kms_key" protoPayload.methodName="Encrypt" OR protoPayload.methodName="Decrypt"```
Elena (security): Exactly — map decrypt events to scan run IDs. Also want to ensure retention is 400 days for compliance. Is that feasible?
Ram (infra): Storage-wise yes. Need to update log-export to bigquery and apply retention. I'll open infra ticket.
Tara (eng): On the SAST finding side, last night's job flagged a proto deserialization issue in ingest-service. I'm triaging but want to tie that finding to the same evidence chain. How do we attach scanner artifacts to a security-review ticket automatically?
Elena (security): We have a small webhook consumer (scanbot) that posts findings to our triage board. If buildkite decrypts and writes metadata, scanbot can attach a signed manifest. Proposed flow: decrypt -> emit JSON manifest (scan_id, artifact_hash, decrypt_audit_id) -> scanbot attaches to Jira ticket.
scanbot: automated: I can already attach artifacts if the manifest is uploaded to /scans/manifests/{scan_id}. Need a service account with write to that bucket and a signed webhook secret.
Tara (eng): perfect. What about RBAC rollback plan? If we accidentally over-perm, what's the safe fast rollback?
Ram (infra): rollback plan: 1) remove IAM binding, 2) rotate key (if concerned), 3) set deny policy on the key for that service account as emergency kill switch. We should document the exact commands in runbook.
Elena (security): also add an audit alert: if the service account decrypts >X artifacts outside a scheduled window, trigger an incident. Can we get that into alerting?
Ram (infra): yes. We'll create a logs-based metric and alert in pagerduty on-call. Threshold suggestion? Tara?
Tara (eng): maybe >20 decrypts per hour outside scheduled window. Fine-tune after 24h.
Elena (security): last item: ownership. I'll be the security owner for the change, Ram will be infra owner, Tara you'll validate the triage attachments. We'll run a canary: enable binding only for a test project/namespace for 48h, verify logs + scanbot attachments, then roll to prod.
Ram (infra): I'll create the canary change PR and the infra ticket with the log-export update and the runbook. ETA EOD tomorrow.
Tara (eng): I'll prepare a tiny integration test that runs a decrypt + manifest upload and verifies scanbot link.
Elena (security): thanks. tagging follow-ups: @ram assign infra/TKT-4582 for log retention + alert, @tara create CI test branch. :thumbsup:
scanbot: automated: noted. I will post a thread update to the triage board when manifest is observed.
